text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawnah says Middle East peace process is going through an uncertain stage and the parties should sit down at the negotiating table again instead of negotiating through the media.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali, returning from Tunis, says Jordan and Tunis have identical views on Arab issues.
- Jordan supports setting up common Arab market, says Deputy Prime Minister Jawad Anani.
- 10 defence witnesses to be heard today in trial of Ahmed Daqamsa, Jordanian soldier who shot dead seven Israeli girls.
- Majali says Jordan supports the holding of Doha economic conference and Jordan has no differences with Syria, which opposes the conference.
- U.S. oil firm Anadorko signs contract with National Oil Company to drill for oil in northeast Jordan.
- Iraq, Syria and Iran are on the path to an alliance, analysts say in Washington.
- King Hussein orders that Iraqi child suffering from leukemia be treated at the king's expense either in Jordan or abroad.
- Anani says agreement with Israel on Aqaba airport has been frozen.
- Daqamsa mentally ill and tried to commit suicide, court hears.
- Government to sell state shares to employees and retired workers at a discount, Anani says.
- First flight between Jordan and Kuwait, expected to fly on July 9, was fully booked within an hour of being announced.
- Government to set up fund for privatisation proceeds.
